newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela's rival to become acting SAfrica president.
newsitem.headline: Mandela's rival to become acting SAfrica president.

text.p: South African opposition leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi gets a second taste of life at the top when he is sworn in as acting president on Sunday, President Nelson Mandela's spokesman said.
"He is a person the president has confidence in and the person he feels will be able to handle the running of the government," Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Reuters.
Buthelezi will take the reins of power in the absence of both President Mandela, who leaves on Monday for India and Bangladesh, and Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who is scheduled to travel to Angola.
Buthelezi, who will be sworn in later on Sunday by the president of South Africa's Constitutional Court, Arthur Chaskalson, relinquishes power on Wednesday when Mbeki returns.
A hereditary Zulu chief, Buthelezi is leader of the Inkatha Freedom Party and a bitter rival of Mandela's ruling party.
In February Buthelezi briefly held the position of acting president when Mbeki and Mandela were both out of the country at the Davos World Economic Forum.
Using Buthelezi as an acting president is widely seen as a gesture of peace and goodwill between Inkatha and Mandela's African National Congress.
